text:
Priya: saw lots of tiny-gang evictions in eu-west1 this morning, multiple customers' jobs restarted.

Mike: timeline? I saw a spike in preemptions around 08:05 UTC.

Priya: yep. snippet from scheduler/provisioner logs:

Priya: ```
W0830 08:05:12 scheduler.go:421] preempting pods for pod=batch-train-42
I0830 08:05:13 provisioner: scale-up triggered for gpu-pool (4 -> 8)
I0830 08:05:14 kubelet: pod batch-train-42 evicted: preemption
```

Anya: provisioning started but nodes didn't become Ready before kubelet evicted local pods. Any AZ mismatch?

Chris: provisioner ended up creating in eu-west1-b despite most pending pods preferring eu-west1-c via strict topology affinity. Cloud API returned 429/insufficient on c, so it fell back to other zones.

Priya: that cross-zone fallback scattered gangs across racks and ended up with many tiny pods occupying single-GPU slots, then preempt waves hit.

Mike: looks like autoscaler/backoff behavior is too aggressive about preempting. We should avoid evicting when a scale-up is in-flight for the same zone.

Anya: options:
- increase provisioner retry/backoff to keep trying same-AZ (slower but preserves locality)
- relax pod affinity for tiny gangs (could hurt perf)
- add a transient scheduler holdback while scale-up stabilizes

Chris: also noticed fragmentation from lots of short-lived tiny pods. They create small holes in GPU allocation making binpacking worse.

Priya: proposal: implement a zone-aware "provision stabilize window" (default 30s) during which scheduler suppresses aggressive preemption for pending pods if a scale-up is observed in the target zone.

Mike: +1 for 30s initially. Also emit a metric `scheduler.provisioner_cooldown_mismatch` so we can alert when preemptions spike during scale-ups.

Anya: gate the behavior per-zone: only suppress if new nodes are provisioned in the same zone as the pending pods.

Chris: config sketch:

Chris: ```yaml
scheduler:
  provisionStabilizeWindow: 30s
  zoneAware: true
```

Priya: opening a small PR to eng-scheduler. tagging @Chris @Mike for review.

Mike: I can review. let's also add a Grafana dashboard: overlay scale-up events, cloud API 429s for flavors, and preemption count.

ops-bot: alert: eu-west1 preemptions > 40 in 5m

sre-oncall: investigating. tailing logs now. so far 3 customer jobs restarted, no elevated 5xx yet.

Priya: will canary the change in staging and replay today's scale-up trace.

Chris: additional long-term idea: create a burst/binary pool for tiny pods so they pack opportunistically into ephemeral shared slots and avoid scattering gang pods across racks.

Mike: cost/latency tradeoff note: burst pool will improve binpacking and reduce cost but we must track QoS. include a latency vs cost curve in the RFC.

Priya: plan: (1) PR with zone-aware 30s stabilize + metric (2) canary in staging with trace replay (3) monitor preemptions + customer impact (4) roll to prod with 1h ramp if green.

Anya: I'll update the runbook with rollback steps.

ops-bot: deployment: scheduler-v2.4.1-canary started in staging

Priya: canary results: during trace replay preemptions dropped ~75%, Ready latency for nodes unchanged, no regression in request latency.

sre-oncall: prod rollout started, will escalate if preemptions > 20/min or customer 5xx spike.

Chris: I'll draft an RFC covering permanent zone-aware provisioner defaults + burst pool proposal and cloud API retry backoff tuning.

Mike: agree. also tune stabilize window after we get real-world data (maybe 15s later if safe).

Priya: PR: https://github.com/redwood/scheduler/pull/842

Priya: dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/scaleup/preemptions-vs-scaleups

sre-oncall: tagging this incident P2 for tracking. will keep thread updated.

Priya: closing once prod is stable. :white_check_mark:
